ROLE

_scorecardTemplateComment: Module 3 -- interview scorecards. Resolution is posting-level first, then department, then the company-wide default, so this set demonstrates all three layers. Criterion types are Rating, YesNo and Text.

scorecardTemplates.name: Company-wide default scorecard
scorecardTemplates.description: Used whenever no department or posting template applies.

criteria.label: Communication
criteria.guidance: Clarity, listening, and whether they check understanding before answering.

criteria.label: Role-relevant experience
criteria.guidance: Depth against what this specific role needs, not seniority in general.

criteria.label: Problem solving
criteria.guidance: How they decompose an unfamiliar problem out loud.

criteria.label: Would you work with them?
criteria.guidance: Answer for the team, not for yourself personally.

criteria.label: Evidence for your rating
criteria.guidance: Quote something they actually said. A rating without evidence is a vote.

scorecardTemplates.name: Engineering interview scorecard
scorecardTemplates.description: Engineering department default, for all technical roles.

criteria.label: Technical depth
criteria.guidance: Do they understand why, not just how? Probe one topic to its limit.

criteria.label: Code quality and testing
criteria.guidance: Do they test behaviour or implementation? Do they notice their own bugs?

criteria.label: System design
criteria.guidance: Trade-offs named explicitly, not just a diagram.

criteria.label: Debugging approach
criteria.guidance: Do they form a hypothesis and test it, or change things at random?

criteria.label: Collaboration
criteria.guidance: How they handle being disagreed with during the interview itself.

criteria.label: Ships to production?
criteria.guidance: Have they owned something real, in front of real users?

criteria.label: Strongest and weakest area
criteria.guidance: Both. A scorecard with no weakness recorded is not a scorecard.

criteria.label: Discovery skill
criteria.guidance: Did they ask you questions, or only pitch?

criteria.label: Objection handling
criteria.guidance: Give them a real objection and watch what they do with it.

criteria.label: Pipeline discipline
criteria.guidance: Can they describe their own funnel with numbers?

criteria.label: Burmese and English
criteria.guidance: Both languages, in a customer-facing register.

criteria.label: Quota history verified?
criteria.guidance: Specific numbers and periods, not 'always exceeded'.

criteria.label: Deal they lost, and why
criteria.guidance: Candidates who cannot name one have not reflected on their own losses.

_interviewComment: Interviews are scheduled only for candidates already at the Interview stage, so the demo data stays internally consistent — no interview exists for someone who never got past screening.
_interviewerRoleBug: Panels deliberately include an Interviewer (intv1/intv2) but no scorecard is authored by one. That is not a modelling choice -- the Interviewer role CANNOT submit a scorecard today. RbacSeedData.cs:158-165 grants it interviews:read, scorecards:read and scorecards:submit, but InterviewsController is gated on Policies.InternalUser, which is RequireRole(Admin, HrDirector, Recruiter, HiringManager, Approver) at Program.cs:66-68 -- Interviewer is absent, so every interview and scorecard endpoint returns 403 to the one role that exists to use them. Scorecards below are therefore authored by a Hiring Manager and a Recruiter, who can. Fix the policy and the Interviewer entries become authorable.
_scorecardComment: Submitted feedback for the completed interview, plus one deliberate draft. Two panel members disagreeing on the same candidate is the point: a demo where every interviewer says StrongYes shows nothing about how the product handles a split panel. Ratings are 1-5; recommendation is one of StrongNo, No, Yes, StrongYes. Answers are matched to criteria by label at seed time, because criterion ids only exist once the template has been created.

_noteComment: Module 3.4 -- collaborative notes with @mentions. A handle is the local part of the user's email, so @susu.hlaing resolves to Ma Su Su Hlaing. Notes marked pinToInterview attach to that interview round rather than to the application generally.

notes.body: Screening call done. Six years in product design, currently owns the design system at an HR SaaS company. Available in four weeks. @aungkyaw.moe her portfolio is the strongest we have had for this role -- worth your time before the panel.
Panel debrief: @susu.hlaing and I disagree on the legacy-codebase question. She rates it a non-issue, I think it is a real ramp-up risk. Not blocking -- flagging so the next round probes it directly.
Read both scorecards. A split panel is fine; what matters is that the disagreement is written down and specific. Proceed to the next round. @susu.hlaing please schedule.
Strong design-systems background but no B2B dashboard work. Keeping at screening until we see whether Ma Ei Phyu Sin converts.

Rejected at screening -- two years experience against a role that needs five. Sent a personal note rather than the template; he asked for feedback and deserves it. Worth revisiting for a junior opening.
Offer stage. Verified quota history with two references: 118% and 104% in the last two years. @nwenwe.win we should move quickly, he has another process running.
First round scheduled. Fluent in both languages -- confirmed on the call, not just claimed on the CV.

Ten years enterprise sales, explicitly wants a player-coach role. We are not hiring a lead here. Holding at screening rather than rejecting -- worth a conversation if the Sales Lead requisition is approved next quarter.
